snippets.output: The duration of seasonal influenza (flu) can vary depending on several factors, including an individual's age, overall health, and the specific strain of the virus.
snippets.pattern_notes: General claim (atom 1) + enumerated factors (2-4). Canonical 'factors include' enumeration.

snippets.output: Seasonal influenza typically lasts about 1–2 weeks, with symptoms ranging from 5–14 days.
Seasonal influenza symptoms can start to improve within 3–4 days after illness onset.
It may take up to 2 weeks for a person to fully recover from seasonal influenza.
Some people with seasonal influenza may experience prolonged illness or complications that can last longer.
Older adults and young children may experience prolonged illness or complications from seasonal influenza.
snippets.pattern_notes: Two parallel at-risk populations sharing same risk.

snippets.output: Antiviral medications, such as Oseltamivir (Tamiflu) and Zanamivir (Relenza), can help shorten the duration and severity of the seasonal influenza when started within 48 hours of symptom onset.
snippets.pattern_notes: Enumerated antiviral benefits (duration, severity) + named examples (Tamiflu, Relenza) + timing qualifier.
